text: Few people may view the Star Trek universe. <break time="0.8s" /> Through an economic lens. <break time="0.8s" /> But doing so provides. <break time="0.8s" /> A window into a world that might soon be upon us. <break time="0.8s" /> All of classical economics is based on the notion. <break time="0.8s" /> That there is not usually enough of anything. <break time="0.8s" /> To give everyone everything they want or need. <break time="0.8s" /> Because of that. <break time="0.8s" /> We use markets and pricing. <break time="0.8s" /> To allocate those goods, services, and resources. <break time="0.8s" /> To where they might result in the highest benefit. <break time="0.8s" /> In Star Trek, however. <break time="0.8s" /> There is not much scarcity. <break time="0.8s" /> Technology has allowed that society. <break time="0.8s" /> To reproduce any food they want. <break time="0.8s" /> Transport themselves thousands of miles. <break time="0.8s" /> In the blink of an eye. <break time="0.8s" /> Communicate over light years. <break time="0.8s" /> And travel among the stars. <break time="0.8s" /> All of humanity in that world. <break time="0.8s" /> Has been fully educated. <break time="0.8s" /> So that they can participate in this prosperity. <break time="0.8s" /> Everyone is an explorer, researcher, engineer, artist, doctor, or counselor. <break time="0.8s" /> Generative AI has the potential. <break time="0.8s" /> To allow many dimensions of our own society. <break time="0.8s" /> To be similarly highly abundant.
